claims.text: UK universities can fund up to 30 Leverhulme Centenary Doctoral Scholarships.
The scholarships must be in an interdisciplinary priority research area for the institution.
The Leverhulme Centenary Doctoral Scholarships are open for submission in March 2026.
The scheme requirements are largely the same as the 2023 round.
This round includes additional studentships.
This round includes funding for postdoctoral opportunities.
This round includes funding for programme administration costs.
The Leverhulme Trust does not accept applications directly from graduates.
Ten awards of up to £5 million will be made to UK universities.
Each award provides funds for 18 four-year Leverhulme Doctoral Scholarships at UK/home rates.
Each award provides funds for 6 four-year Scholarships at international/overseas rates.
8 scholarships are to be offered in each year of the first three years of the grant.
Universities can apply for additional funding for up to six students from underrepresented groups (low income and Black students) to undertake a master’s degree before progressing to a PhD.
Each grant runs over a period of 9 years.
The scheme is open to applications from any UK university that holds research degree awarding powers in its own right.
Applications will be accepted from a consortium of a maximum of two universities.
One university and one principal applicant must be identified to lead in a consortium application.
A university may submit only one application as lead.
A university may partner in multiple applications, provided they are in different disciplinary areas.
Institutions may also recruit six students to a master’s plus PhD programme in addition to the 24 standard PhD scholarships.
Students wishing to pursue the master’s plus PhD route must be a UK domiciled student.
Students wishing to pursue the master’s plus PhD route must not already have a master’s degree from the host institution.
Students wishing to pursue the master’s plus PhD route must be from a low-income household background.
Students wishing to pursue the master’s plus PhD route can be from specific Black or Mixed ethnicity categories.
UK students undertaking a PhD will be eligible for a fixed sum scholarship for up to 48 months of full-time doctoral study.
UK PhD scholarships cover maintenance at UKRI base levels.
UK PhD scholarships cover tuition fees at UKRI base levels.
UK PhD scholarships include £10,000 for research and training needs.
Up to six fixed sum scholarships can be made to international students for up to 48 months of full-time doctoral study.
International PhD scholarships cover maintenance at UKRI base levels.
International PhD scholarships cover tuition fees at the university’s standard international fee rate, up to a maximum of £25,000 per year.
International PhD scholarships include £10,000 for research and training needs.
Universities can apply for up to six further studentships for a master’s plus doctoral programme.
Each master’s plus PhD scholarship covers up to 60 months of full-time study.
Master’s plus PhD research master’s degree component covers maintenance at UKRI base level.
Master’s plus PhD research master’s degree component covers tuition fees up to a maximum of £12,000.
Master’s plus PhD doctoral degree component covers maintenance at UKRI base levels.
Master’s plus PhD doctoral degree component covers tuition fees at UKRI base levels.
Master’s plus PhD doctoral degree component includes £10,000 for research and training needs.
Funds for master's plus PhD students are ring-fenced for supporting students from underrepresented groups.
£75,000 of ring-fenced funding will be made available to support cohort-building activities.
Up to £400,000 of ring-fenced funding is available to support postdoctoral opportunities for LCDS programme graduates.
Universities may request up to £225,000 of funding for dedicated administrative support.
The awards are offered in a subject area or thematic area identified as a research priority by applicant universities.
The chosen area should be broad enough to sustain up to 30 doctoral students over the grant period.
The chosen area should have a clear and coherent overarching thematic identity.
Applications are not accepted from other UK institutions or organisations.
Applications must be submitted by a principal applicant.
For consortium proposals, a single principal applicant should be identified.
The application procedure involves a short application form and a detailed programme description.
A supporting statement from a designated representative of the university is required.
For consortium applications, supporting statements are required from both participating universities.
The Trust expects demonstrable commitment from the host institution(s) for the proposed doctoral centre.
There is no requirement for the university to offer matched studentships in this round.
The short application form requires brief biographical details about the principal applicant.
The short application form requires the title of the programme.
The short application form requires a 250-word summary of the rationale behind the choice of research subject area.
The short application form requires a 250-word summary of the relationship between the proposed scholarships and current doctoral training awards.
The short application form requires a 250-word summary of how the scholarships would provide added value.
The short application form requires a 250-word summary of how the doctoral scholars would be supervised and trained.
The short application form requires a 250-word summary of the legacy that will be delivered and how it will be sustained.
The short application form requires a 250-word summary of details of additional financial or other support resources provided.
The detailed programme description should address the rationale behind the choice of research subject area.
The detailed programme description should address the relationship between the proposed scholarships and current doctoral training awards.
The detailed programme description should address how the scholarships would add value.
The detailed programme description should address the proposed mode of selecting Leverhulme Doctoral Scholars.
The detailed programme description should address the proposed mode of identifying and selecting Master’s Plus Doctoral Scholars.
The detailed programme description should address how scholars would be supervised and progress monitored.
The detailed programme description should describe plans for training and cohort-building activities.
The detailed programme description should include relevant information about key academic staff and research capacity.
The detailed programme description should outline how the proposed Doctoral Scholarship would utilise and administer the post-doctoral support element.
The detailed programme description should address the legacy that will be delivered and how it will be sustained.
For consortium applications, the detailed programme description must include the basis and history of the partnership and expected benefits.
For consortium applications, the detailed programme description must include a description of how the award would be managed across partners.
For consortium applications, the detailed programme description must include a contingency plan if a partner university cannot continue.
The maximum length of the detailed programme description statement is 10 sides of A4.
The supporting statement should be no more than 500 words.
The supporting statement should explain why the research subject area is important to the university.
The supporting statement should provide key information about the university’s research capacity in the area.
The supporting statement should demonstrate how the institution will provide an appropriate level of commitment to the programme.
Consortium applications should submit a letter of support from the partner institution.
The partner university's letter of support should address the points required for the supporting statement from the lead institution.
The partner university's letter of support should be signed, dated, and on headed paper.
Once the designated representative of the lead university has provided the statement, the application form requires online institutional approval.
There is no additional approval stage for the partner university in consortium applications.
